page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Storage includes a bundled 225 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network capability.

Benchmark data reflects clear strengths in GPU-centric machine learning tasks. Large language model inference speeds reach the top tier (top 10%) for prompt processing on smaller models (8447.43 tokens/sec on 135M) and medium models (1163.92 tokens/sec on 7B). Text generation throughput is strong (top 25%), recording 40.25 tokens/sec on a 7B model. However, on large 70B parameter models, prompt processing drops to average tier (13.51 tokens/sec), constrained by the 16 GB VRAM limit.

Host CPU execution demonstrates moderate to lower performance metrics. Single-core stress-ng (1286.18) and Geekbench (1144.0) fall into the bottom 25%, as do compression benchmarks like single-threaded gzip (21.73 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core operations land consistently in the middle 50%, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7019.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14414.98. General memory operations and caching throughput are similarly positioned within average bands.

The hardware configuration provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for targeted acceleration tasks that do not justify high-end A100 or H100 accelerators. The inclusion of bundled local NVMe storage and high networking bandwidth supports data-intensive local operations. The instance is well matched for mid-sized LLM inference, ML model serving, video transcoding, graphics processing, and auxiliary web application backend tasks.

Benchmark metrics indicate average multi-core CPU capacity and weaker single-thread throughput, but strong performance in GPU-driven inference. Specifically, it delivers top-tier prompt processing on 135M and 7B parameter models, alongside strong text generation throughput. The instance offers a balanced resource density for machine learning inference, graphics processing, video streaming, and data pipelines where large-scale enterprise accelerators are unnecessary.
